options.name: adpttimeout
options.description: Adapts the configured request timeout based on flow conditions. The timeout is increased or decreased internally and applied on the flow.

options.name: allowonlywordcharactersandhyphen
options.description: When enabled allows only the word characters [A-Za-z0-9_] and hyphen [-] in the request/response header names and the connection will be reset for the other characters. When disabled allows any visible (printing) characters (%21-%7E) except delimiters (double quotes and "(),/:;<=>?@[]{}").

options.name: altsvc
options.description: Choose whether to enable support for Alternative Services.

options.name: altsvcvalue
options.description: Configure a custom Alternative Services header value that should be inserted in the response to advertise a HTTP/SSL/HTTP_QUIC vserver.

options.name: apdexcltresptimethreshold
options.description: This option sets the satisfactory threshold (T) for client response time in milliseconds to be used for APDEX calculations. This means a transaction responding in less than this threshold is considered satisfactory. Transaction responding between T and 4*T is considered tolerable. Any transaction responding in more than 4*T time is considered frustrating. Citrix ADC maintains stats for such tolerable and frustrating transcations. And client response time related apdex counters are only updated o

options.name: api_path
options.description: Base NITRO API path. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: clientiphdrexpr
options.description: Name of the header that contains the real client IP address.

options.name: cmponpush
options.description: Start data compression on receiving a TCP packet with PUSH flag set.

options.name: conmultiplex
options.description: Reuse server connections for requests from more than one client connections.

options.name: dropextracrlf
options.description: Drop any extra 'CR' and 'LF' characters present after the header.

options.name: dropextradata
options.description: Drop any extra data when server sends more data than the specified content-length.

options.name: dropinvalreqs
options.description: Drop invalid HTTP requests or responses.

options.name: grpcholdlimit
options.description: Maximum size in bytes allowed to buffer gRPC packets till trailer is received

options.name: grpcholdtimeout
options.description: Maximum time in milliseconds allowed to buffer gRPC packets till trailer is received. The value should be in multiples of 100

options.name: grpclengthdelimitation
options.description: Set to C(DISABLED) for gRPC without a length delimitation.

options.name: hostheadervalidation
options.description: Validates the length of the Host header and its syntax. Also includes validation of the port number if specified

options.name: http2
options.description: Choose whether to enable support for HTTP/2.

options.name: http2altsvcframe
options.description: Choose whether to enable support for sending HTTP/2 ALTSVC frames. When enabled, the ADC sends HTTP/2 ALTSVC frames to HTTP/2 clients, instead of the Alt-Svc response header field. Not applicable to servers.

options.name: http2direct
options.description: Choose whether to enable support for Direct HTTP/2.

options.name: http2extendedconnect
options.description: Choose whether to enable HTTP/2 Extended CONNECT mechanism.

options.name: http2headertablesize
options.description: Maximum size of the header compression table used to decode header blocks, in bytes.

options.name: http2initialconnwindowsize
options.description: Initial window size for connection level flow control, in bytes.

options.name: http2initialwindowsize
options.description: Initial window size for stream level flow control, in bytes.

options.name: http2maxconcurrentstreams
options.description: Maximum number of concurrent streams that is allowed per connection.

options.name: http2maxemptyframespermin
options.description: Maximum number of empty frames allowed in HTTP2 connection per minute

options.name: http2maxframesize
options.description: Maximum size of the frame payload that the Citrix ADC is willing to receive, in bytes.

options.name: http2maxheaderlistsize
options.description: Maximum size of header list that the Citrix ADC is prepared to accept, in bytes. NOTE: The actual plain text header size that the Citrix ADC accepts is limited by maxHeaderLen. Please change maxHeaderLen parameter as well when modifying http2MaxHeaderListSize.

options.name: http2maxpingframespermin
options.description: Maximum number of PING frames allowed in HTTP2 connection per minute

options.name: http2maxresetframespermin
options.description: Maximum number of outgoing RST_STREAM frames allowed in HTTP/2 connection per minute

options.name: http2maxrxresetframespermin
options.description: Maximum number of incoming RST_STREAM frames allowed in HTTP/2 connection per minute

options.name: http2maxsettingsframespermin
options.description: Maximum number of SETTINGS frames allowed in HTTP2 connection per minute

options.name: http2minseverconn
options.description: Minimum number of HTTP2 connections established to backend server, on receiving HTTP requests from client before multiplexing the streams into the available HTTP/2 connections.

options.name: http2smallwndtimeout
options.description: Timeout, in seconds, for HTTP/2 small-window stalled streams. Introduced in firmware 14.1-72.61 to mitigate CVE-2026-13474.

options.name: http2strictcipher
options.description: Choose whether to enable strict HTTP/2 cipher selection

options.name: http3
options.description: Choose whether to enable support for HTTP/3.

options.name: http3maxheaderblockedstreams
options.description: Maximum number of HTTP/3 streams that can be blocked while HTTP/3 headers are being decoded.

options.name: http3maxheaderfieldsectionsize
options.description: Maximum size of the HTTP/3 header field section, in bytes.

options.name: http3maxheadertablesize
options.description: Maximum size of the HTTP/3 QPACK dynamic header table, in bytes.

options.name: http3minseverconn
options.description: Minimum number of HTTP/3 connections established to backend server, on receiving HTTP requests from client before multiplexing the streams into the available HTTP/3 connections.

options.name: http3webtransport
options.description: Choose whether to enable support for WebTransport over HTTP/3.

options.name: httppipelinebuffsize
options.description: Application pipeline request buffering size, in bytes.

options.name: incomphdrdelay
options.description: Maximum time to wait, in milliseconds, between incomplete header packets. If the header packets take longer to arrive at Citrix ADC, the connection is silently dropped.

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_id
options.description: The ID of the managed NetScaler instance to which NetScaler Console has to configure as a proxy server. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_ip
options.description: The IP of the managed NetScaler instance to which NetScaler Console has to configure as a proxy server. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_name
options.description: The name of the managed NetScaler instance to which NetScaler Console has to configure as a proxy server. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_password
options.description: The password of the managed NetScaler instance. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call In Settings > Administration > System Configurations > Basic Settings, if you select Prompt Credentials for Instance Login, ensure to configure username and password of a managed instance.

options.name: managed_netscaler_instance_username
options.description: The username of the managed NetScaler instance. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call In Settings > Administration > System Configurations > Basic Settings, if you select Prompt Credentials for Instance Login, ensure to configure username and password of a managed instance.

options.name: markconnreqinval
options.description: Mark CONNECT requests as invalid.

options.name: markhttp09inval
options.description: Mark HTTP/0.9 requests as invalid.

options.name: markhttpheaderextrawserror
options.description: Mark Http header with extra white space as invalid

options.name: markrfc7230noncompliantinval
options.description: Mark RFC7230 non-compliant transaction as invalid

options.name: marktracereqinval
options.description: Mark TRACE requests as invalid.

options.name: maxduplicateheaderfields
options.description: Maximum number of allowed occurrences of header fields that share the same field name. This threshold is enforced only for well-known header field names recognized by NetScaler. If the value is set to 0, then it will be similar to previous behavior, Where we store only 15 duplicate headers and rest are parsed and send to the server.

options.name: maxheaderfieldlen
options.description: Number of bytes allowed for header field for HTTP header. If number of bytes exceeds beyond configured value, then request will be marked invalid

options.name: maxheaderlen
options.description: Number of bytes to be queued to look for complete header before returning error. If complete header is not obtained after queuing these many bytes, request will be marked as invalid and no L7 processing will be done for that TCP connection.

options.name: maxreq
options.description: Maximum number of requests allowed on a single connection. Zero implies no limit on the number of requests.

options.name: maxreusepool
options.description: Maximum limit on the number of connections, from the Citrix ADC to a particular server that are kept in the reuse pool. This setting is helpful for optimal memory utilization and for reducing the idle connections to the server just after the peak time. Zero implies no limit on reuse pool size. If non-zero value is given, it has to be greater than or equal to the number of running Packet Engines.

options.name: minreusepool
options.description: Minimum limit on the number of connections, from the Citrix ADC to a particular server that are kept in the reuse pool. This setting is helpful for optimal memory utilization and for reducing the idle connections to the server just after the peak time. Zero implies no limit on reuse pool size.

options.name: name
options.description: Name for an HTTP profile. Must begin with a letter, number, or the underscore \(_\) character. Other characters allowed, after the first character, are the hyphen \(-\), period \(.\), hash \(\#\), space \( \), at \(@\), colon \(:\), and equal \(=\) characters. The name of a HTTP profile cannot be changed after it is created.  CLI Users: If the name includes one or more spaces, enclose the name in double or single quotation marks \(for example, "my http profile" or 'my http profile'\).

options.name: netscaler_console_as_proxy_server
options.description: The IP address of the NetScaler ADC appliance acting as a proxy server. Define only in case of an ADM service proxy call

options.name: nitro_auth_token
options.description: The authentication token provided by a login operation.

options.name: nitro_pass
options.description: The password with which to authenticate to the NetScaler ADC node.

options.name: nitro_protocol
options.description: Which protocol to use when accessing the nitro API objects.

options.name: nitro_user
options.description: The username with which to authenticate to the NetScaler ADC node.

options.name: nsip
options.description: The ip address of the NetScaler ADC appliance where the nitro API calls will be made. The port can be specified with the colon (:). E.g. 192.168.1.1:555.

options.name: passprotocolupgrade
options.description: Pass protocol upgrade request to the server.

options.name: persistentetag
options.description: Generate the persistent Citrix ADC specific ETag for the HTTP response with ETag header.

options.name: remove_non_updatable_params
options.description: When given yes, the module will remove any parameters that are not updatable in the resource. If no, the module will return error if any non-updatable parameters are provided.

options.name: reqtimeout
options.description: Time, in seconds, within which the HTTP request must complete. If the request does not complete within this time, the specified request timeout action is executed. Zero disables the timeout.

options.name: reqtimeoutaction
options.description: Action to take when the HTTP request does not complete within the specified request timeout duration. You can configure the following actions: * RESET - Send RST (reset) to client when timeout occurs. * DROP - Drop silently when timeout occurs. * Custom responder action - Name of the responder action to trigger when timeout occurs, used to send custom message.

options.name: reusepooltimeout
options.description: Idle timeout (in seconds) for server connections in re-use pool. Connections in the re-use pool are flushed, if they remain idle for the configured timeout.

options.name: rtsptunnel
options.description: Allow RTSP tunnel in HTTP. Once application/x-rtsp-tunnelled is seen in Accept or Content-Type header, Citrix ADC does not process Layer 7 traffic on this connection.

options.name: save_config
options.description: If C(true) the module will save the configuration on the NetScaler ADC node if it makes any changes. The module will not save the configuration on the NetScaler ADC node if it made no changes.

options.name: state
options.description: The state of the resource being configured by the module on the NetScaler ADC node. When C(present), the resource will be added/updated configured according to the module's parameters. When C(absent), the resource will be deleted from the NetScaler ADC node. When C(unset), the resource will be unset on the NetScaler ADC node.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: If C(false), SSL certificates will not be validated. This should only be used on personally controlled sites using self-signed certificates.

options.name: weblog
options.description: Enable or disable web logging.

options.name: websocket
options.description: HTTP connection to be upgraded to a web socket connection. Once upgraded, Citrix ADC does not process Layer 7 traffic on this connection.
